newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait to shed stake in local securities firm.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait to shed stake in local securities firm.

text.p: Kuwait plans to sell off most of its majority stake in the Securities Group, the official Kuwait News Agency reported on Monday.
"Kuwait Investment Authority (KIA) announced today (Monday) that it will offer 80 million shares of its equity in Securities Group for sale in a public auction," the agency said.
KIA, the state investment arm, will also sell another 220 shares through public subscription after an auction in October, said the agency without specifing the auction date.
The starting price for the auction is 136 fils ($0.45) per share which would earn the state a minimum of 10.8 million dinars. There are 1,000 fils to the dinar.
State-controlled Securities Group is one of the leading securities firms in Kuwait.
The rest of the shares will be sold at a price to be determined after the auction, said the agency.
KIA's stake in Securities Group amounts to 95 percent of its issued shares. The firm's paid up capital is 33 million dinars.
The agency said the 300 million shares to be sold make up 91 percent of the firm's issued shares.
Kuwait has announced plans to sell its holdings in some 60 local firms and shed stakes in some public services such as water, electricity and telecommunications.
KIA said in May state revenue from its privatisation plan mobilised in 1994 stood at over 350 million dinars so far.

Participation in Kuwait's privatisation plan is exclusive to nationals of the Gulf Cooperation Council, a military, economic and political alliance that also groups Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman and Bahrain.
